display.purpose: Large public and member statements, route numerals, and short declarations.

headline.purpose: Section titles that need strong scanning without competing with the hero.

title.purpose: Day names, list titles, and compact records.

body.purpose: Explanatory copy, forms, instructions, and data descriptions.

label.purpose: Navigation, route numbers, status labels, and short control text.

action.purpose: The decisive next step, set larger than route labels and kept short.

shadows.name: waypoint-ambient
shadows.purpose: Reserved for route waypoint controls so they remain legible over contour surfaces.

shadows.name: notice-ambient
shadows.purpose: Reserved for transient install or status notices that sit above the page.

motion.name: static-companion
motion.purpose: Companion art is static by default and remains static in reduced motion.

motion.name: reduced-motion-collapse
motion.purpose: The global reduced-motion contract removes movement without removing state or content.

breakpoints.name: phone
breakpoints.purpose: Stack content, use fixed bottom navigation, and collapse rollout Library, editor, History, Settings, and runner slots.

breakpoints.name: tablet
breakpoints.purpose: Introduce two-column content grids and permit the guarded Settings slot while rollout Library, editor, History, and runner art stays collapsed.

breakpoints.name: desktop
breakpoints.purpose: Move navigation into the header and reserve broad heading-side space for eligible companion art outside task and data planes.

components.name: Primary Action
components.description: A coral, square-edged action for the next decisive task.
components.css: .ds-primary-action { align-items: center; background: var(--coral); border: 0; color: var(--on-coral); cursor: pointer; display: inline-flex; font-family: var(--font-display); font-size: 1.3rem; font-weight: 600; justify-content: space-between; letter-spacing: .04em; min-height: 3.6rem; padding: .8rem 1rem; text-transform: uppercase; } .ds-primary-action:hover { background: var(--coral-strong); } .ds-primary-action:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--focus); outline-offset: 4px; } .ds-primary-action:active { transform: translateY(1px); }

components.name: Paper Sheet
components.description: A square-edged contained sheet for a readable group of related facts or actions.
components.html:
ROUTE NOTE

Current routine

Keep the next step visible and the explanation nearby.
components.css: .ds-paper-card { background: var(--white); border: 1px solid var(--rule); color: var(--ink); padding: clamp(1rem, 4vw, 2rem); } .ds-paper-card h2 { font-family: var(--font-display); font-size: clamp(2rem, 5vw, 3.8rem); line-height: .9; margin: .55rem 0 1rem; text-transform: uppercase; } .ds-paper-card p { color: var(--ink-soft); line-height: 1.5; margin: 0; max-width: 58ch; } .ds-label { color: var(--lichen); font-family: var(--font-display); letter-spacing: .05em; text-transform: uppercase; }

components.name: Input Field
components.description: A square field for a named, readable input with an explicit focus ring.
components.css: .ds-field { color: var(--ink); display: grid; gap: .35rem; } .ds-field > span { font-family: var(--font-display); letter-spacing: .04em; text-transform: uppercase; } .ds-field input { background: var(--white); border: 1px solid var(--rule); border-radius: 0; color: var(--ink); min-height: 3.4rem; padding: .7rem; } .ds-field input:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--focus); outline-offset: 4px; } .ds-field input::placeholder { color: var(--ink-soft); opacity: 1; }

components.name: Responsive Navigation
components.description: A compact route navigation that is fixed on phones and inline in the desktop header.
components.html: HOMELIBRARYPROGRESSMY WORKOUTS
components.css: .ds-nav { background: var(--ink); color: var(--paper); display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(4, 1fr); padding: .55rem max(.5rem, env(safe-area-inset-left)) calc(.55rem + env(safe-area-inset-bottom)) max(.5rem, env(safe-area-inset-right)); } .ds-nav a { align-items: center; display: flex; font-family: var(--font-display); font-size: .77rem; justify-content: center; letter-spacing: .05em; min-height: 3.5rem; padding: .35rem .2rem; text-decoration: none; text-transform: uppercase; } .ds-nav a:hover { color: var(--coral-on-ink); } .ds-nav a:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--focus); outline-offset: -4px; } .ds-nav a[aria-current="page"] { color: var(--coral-on-ink); }

components.name: Status Stamp
components.description: A compact, text-led state stamp for visible compatibility or action context.
components.html: SAMPLE DATA · NOT YOUR HISTORY
components.css: .ds-status-stamp { border: 2px solid var(--coral); color: var(--coral-strong); display: inline-grid; font-family: var(--font-display); letter-spacing: .04em; padding: .65rem .8rem; text-transform: uppercase; } .ds-status-stamp:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--focus); outline-offset: 4px; }

components.name: Corner Companion Slot
components.description: A decorative, inert, source-faithful animal vignette from the closed eight-variant registry in a reserved slot outside the semantic data plane.
components.css: .ds-companion-slot { align-items: center; background: var(--paper); display: grid; height: var(--companion-slot-block-mobile); justify-items: center; overflow: hidden; pointer-events: none; width: 100%; } .ds-companion-slot[hidden] { display: none; } .ds-companion-slot img { aspect-ratio: 1; block-size: 100%; display: block; inline-size: 100%; max-inline-size: var(--companion-slot-inline); object-fit: contain; pointer-events: none; } @media (forced-colors: active) { .ds-companion-slot { display: none; } } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-companion-slot img { animation: none; transform: none; transition: none; } }

narrative.overview:
My Workout Pal is a warm field-atlas interface: mineral paper, deep blue-green ink, crisp route marks, and coral decisions make planning and logging feel grounded rather than gamified. The visual system keeps the route grammar from `docs/design/DIRECTION.md`—waypoints, ruled sheets, stamped states, and contour surfaces—while keeping the user's task and product truth ahead of decoration.

The selected Corner Companions direction extends that world with one purpose-built, text-free animal vignette in reserved quiet space, with a surface-specific asset and visibility contract. The approved pilot keeps the planning hedgehog on the guest landing, preparing fox on the signed-in personal home, and an opaque reviewing raccoon on the guest Progress preview. The Wave 3 rollout adds the cataloging otter to public and member Library headings, the routine-drafting beaver to the owned editor, the history-archive tortoise to History list and detail, the settings-packing hare to a verified, identity-ready, clean, neutral Settings heading on tablet and desktop, and the workout-corner bear to a recovered, online, neutral runner overview at broad widths. The composite concept board remains evidence, not a shipping asset.
keyCharacteristics: Warm mineral paper and contour texture with restrained ruled dividers.
Condensed display type for route labels and humanist sans serif for reading and entry.
Coral action, lichen compatibility, and deep ink navigation with non-color semantics.
Contextual companions vary by surface while staying outside the data and interaction plane.

rules.name: The One Companion Rule
rules.body: Each eligible surface may use one complete, purpose-built companion vignette as context; the image never carries account, workout, sample-data, progress, or completion meaning.

rules.name: The Semantic Contrast Rule
rules.body: Color may reinforce a state, but ownership, verification, sample disclosure, save outcome, and failure must remain legible in words and structure.

rules.name: The Label/Reading Split Rule
rules.body: Use the condensed face to scan a route or state; use the humanist face to explain what the state means and what the user can do next.

rules.name: The Tonal Layer Rule
rules.body: Prefer paper, deep paper, ink, and rules to extra cards or shadows; add a shadow only when it clarifies a floating or selected interaction.

dos: Do keep the field-atlas palette, condensed display silhouette, humanist reading copy, and ruled structure consistent across public and member surfaces.
Do keep adjacent text and controls authoritative: the neutral `Progress` title and `Sample data · not your history` disclosure must remain the truth for the guest preview.

Do use exactly one purpose-built, text-free animal vignette per eligible surface, apply its surface-specific state contract, and keep it outside text, fields, charts, disclosures, errors, timers, controls, and navigation.

Do preserve each WebP's same-basename provenance record under `docs/design/provenance/companions/`; keep the public companion directory free of JSON sidecars and keep public assets separate from authenticated HTML and data caches.
Do collapse decorative art without a layout gap on image failure or forced colors, and keep it static under reduced motion.
Do treat the selected Corner Companions board as directional evidence only; use the eight purpose-built variants registered by `DecorativeCompanion` in `public/illustrations/companions/`.
Do keep Settings and runner visibility exceptions local to those surfaces and their verified state predicates.
donts: Don't crop, extract, or reuse a character from the composite gym illustration or the Corner Companions board.
Don't put lettering, numbers, sample values, private data, logos, emoji, CSS art, or handmade SVG art inside a companion image.
Don't make a decorative animal the only signal for account identity, verification, saved activity, progress, completion, or failure.
Don't turn the guest Progress preview into a personal-history claim, or the personal home into a sample-data surface.
Don't let companion art cover account chrome, fixed navigation, controls, charts, disclosure, errors, timers, or the primary action.
Don't copy Library's public-cache eligibility to owned/private companions or private routes.
Don't introduce generic floating dashboards, gratuitous rounded cards, photorealism, gradients, glass, or mascot-led promotion into this system.
